::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[How do I determine whether the orientation of a basis is positive or negative using the cross product](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2675132/how-do-i-determine-whether-the-orientation-of-a-basis-is-positive-or-negative-us), asked by [Chisq](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/480197/chisq) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2018-03-03; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I know that if I have an orthonormal base in $\mathbb{R}^3$, namely $e_1$, $e_2$ & $e_3$, then it is positively oriented if
>
> $$e_1 \times e_2 = e_3$$
> $$e_2 \times e_3 = e_1$$
> $$e_3 \times e_1 = e_2$$
>
> It would make sense if it was negatively oriented when
>
> $$e_1 \times e_2 = -e_3$$
> $$e_2 \times e_3 = -e_1$$
> $$e_3 \times e_1 = -e_2$$
>
> But I would like to be sure. Am I correct?
:::

A basis $u$, $v$, $w$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$ is positively oriented if $(u\times v)\cdot w > 0$, and negatively oriented if $(u \times v) \cdot w < 0$.  In the case of orthonormal vectors, that is probably equivalent to what you have.
